questions.subtopic: People by Personality: Optimist vs Pessimist
questions.question:
Select the correct one-word substitution:
"A person who always expects good things to happen and looks on the positive side of life."
questions.explanation: Rule RC-02 ke anusaar, definition 'A person who...' pooch rahi hai, isliye answer ek agent noun hona chahiye. 'Optimist' wo vyakti hota hai jo hamesha positive parinaam expect karta hai. 'Optimistic' adjective hai aur 'Pessimist' opposite meaning deta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02: Person vs Quality / Condition Grammatical Concord.
questions.hint: Check karein ki options mein se kaunsa word person (agent noun) ko represent karta hai aur positive outlook dikhata hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L17

questions.subtopic: Life Writing Formats: Autobiography vs Biography
questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate word for:
"An account of a person's life written by that person themselves."
questions.explanation: Greek prefix 'Auto-' ka matlab 'self' hota hai. Jab koi vyakti apne jeevan ki kahani khud likhta hai, toh use 'Autobiography' (Atmakatha) kehte hain. Agar koi doosra likhe toh wo 'Biography' (Jeevani) hoti hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Definition vs Synonym Precision Rule.
questions.hint: Prefix 'Auto-' par focus karein jiska matlab 'self' (swayam) hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L17

questions.question:
What is the single-word substitution for:
"A person who claims that human intellect cannot know whether God exists or not?"
questions.explanation: Agnostic wo vyakti hai jo kehta hai ki Ishwar ke astitva ka gyan sambhav ya pramanit nahi hai (gnosis = knowledge). Atheist God ke astitva ko reject karta hai, jabki Agnostic knowledge ko unknowable maanta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Definition vs Synonym Precision Rule.
questions.hint: Ye vyakti God ke astitva ko deny nahi kar raha, balki kehta hai ki hum jaan nahi sakte (unknown/unknowable).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L17

questions.question:
Identify the correct term:
"An independent official chosen by disputing parties to settle their conflict with a binding legal award."
questions.explanation: Rule RC-05 ke anusaar, 'Arbitrator' ek independent adjudicator hota hai jo binding order (Arbitral Award) deta hai. Mediator sirf samjhauta karwata hai aur uska faisla binding nahi hota.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Dispute Resolution Roles: Arbitrator vs Mediator.
questions.hint: Definition mein 'BINDING legal award' clue hai; arbitrator binding faisla deta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L17

questions.question:
Which of the following words means:
"A place where bees are kept in hives for scientific collection of honey?"
questions.explanation: Rule RC-03 ke anusaar, Latin root 'apis' (bee) se 'Apiary' banta hai. 'Avis' (bird) se 'Aviary' banta hai. Isliye bees ke liye Apiary sahi answer hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Spatial Enclosure Law: Place vs Occupant vs Activity.
questions.hint: Mnemonic: 'P' in Apiary = Pollination / Bees. 'V' in Aviary = Volant / Birds.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L17

questions.subtopic: Memorial Literature: Epitaph vs Eulogy vs Elegy
questions.question:
Choose the word that accurately replaces:
"A solemn poem or lamentation written to mourn the death of someone."
questions.explanation: Rule RC-06 ke anusaar, nidhan par dukh vyakt karne wali POEM ko 'Elegy' kehte hain. Prashansa bhashan ko 'Eulogy' aur qabr par likhe lekh ko 'Epitaph' kehte hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: Literary & Memorial Triad: Epitaph vs Eulogy vs Elegy.
questions.hint: Definition mein genre 'POEM' (kavita) hai, speech ya stone inscription nahi.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L17

questions.subtopic: Time Intervals: Annual vs Biannual vs Biennial
questions.question:
What is the single-word substitution for:
"Occurring or published twice in a single year?"
questions.explanation: Rule RC-07 ke anusaar, ek hi saal mein do baar hone wali ghatna ko 'Biannual' (or semiannual) kehte hain. 'Biennial' do saal mein ek baar hone wali ghatna hoti hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: Time & Frequency Calculation: Annual vs Biannual vs Biennial.
questions.hint: Twice in ONE year = Biannual. Once every TWO years = Biennial.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L17

questions.question:
Select the correct word for:
"A person who departs from their native country in order to live permanently in another."
questions.explanation: Rule RC-09 ke anusaar, jo vyakti apna desh chhod kar bahar jata hai wo 'Emigrant' (E for Exit) hota hai. Naye desh mein aakar basne wala 'Immigrant' (I for In) kahlata hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Migration Directional Vectors: Immigrant vs Emigrant vs Refugee.
questions.hint: Focus on the direction: DEPARTS from / LEAVES own country = Emigrant.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L17

questions.question:
Which word accurately means:
"To formally clear someone from a criminal charge by a judicial verdict of not guilty?"
questions.explanation: Rule RC-10 ke anusaar, courtroom trial mein criminal charge se nirdosh paakar bari karna 'Acquit' kahlata hai. 'Absolve' paap ya moral blame se release hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Judicial Verdicts & Culpability: Acquit vs Absolve vs Convict.
questions.hint: Definition mein 'court of law / criminal charge' judicial context hai, isliye specific court term chunein.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L17

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the correct substitution:
"Dark thunderstorm clouds gathered on the horizon, signaling that a deluge was ________."
questions.explanation: Rule RC-13 ke anusaar, 'Imminent' ka matlab hota hai jo bohot jald ghatit hone wala ho (impending / about to happen). 'Eminent' prasiddh vyakti hota hai, aur 'Immanent' bheetar antarnihit hona.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-13: Phonetic Lookalike Trap: Imminent vs Immanent vs Eminent.
questions.hint: Sentence keh raha hai ki toofan bohot jald aane wala tha (about to happen).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L17

questions.question:
What is the single-word substitution for:
"A system of government where political power is controlled exclusively by the rich?"
questions.explanation: Greek root 'ploutos' (wealth) + 'kratos' (rule) se 'Plutocracy' banta hai, jiska matlab ameeron ka shasan hota hai. Aristocracy noble birth ka shasan hai aur Theocracy religious leaders ka.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Morphological Root Word Decoding.
questions.hint: Root 'Ploutos' ka matlab wealth hota hai; rule by the wealthy = Plutocracy.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L17

questions.question:
Select the correct substitution for:
"To make something painful, harmful, or bad less severe or intense."
questions.explanation: Rule RC-12 ke anusaar, kisi taklif ya samasya ki tivrata ko kam karne ko 'Mitigate' kehte hain. Aggravate aur Exacerbate sthiti ko aur kharab (worse) banana hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-12: Severity Modulation: Mitigate vs Ameliorate vs Exacerbate.
questions.hint: Tivrata ko kam karna (reduce severity) = Mitigate.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L17
